gap: No result ChatGPT got states that turning a cart you already own into a lithium cart costs $1,149.99 (Redodo 48V 100Ah kit) to $1,579.99 (Vatrer 48V 105Ah kit with UL 2271 in its title) at the makers' US stores today. A new lithium cart costs $10,099 and up: Club Car Onward 2 Passenger starting MSRP, or $11,645 for the cheapest E-Z-GO ELiTE lithium cart at Advantage Golf Cars.
standout_why: I compared against the cited clubcar.com/en-us/personal/golf-carts page, which lists whole-cart MSRPs only ($10,099 to $16,199 for Onward). It does not say whether lithium is standard or what it adds to the price. I also checked clubcar.com/en/lithium-ion, which has no prices and no kWh, range or warranty term. The two cited T&T Golf Carts pages showed no listings when opened (inventory loads in the browser), so ChatGPT's $9,995 RXV figure can't be checked. ChatGPT's own answer offers 'Upgrade an existing golf cart battery' as a follow-up but gives no kit or price. None of these pages prices a lithium conversion kit.
decides: The question splits into two buys. A shopper who already owns a 48V Club Car, E-Z-GO, Yamaha or ICON cart pays about 11–16% of a new lithium cart's price for a 5.1–5.4 kWh kit with a matched charger (the Redodo and Vatrer kits Dealectric lists). A new cart only wins if they have no cart to convert. For new carts, the lowest ELiTE lithium prices I could open are $11,645 for a 2-seat RXV 2 Freedom ELiTE 2.2 and $11,999 for a 4-seat 2027 Liberty 4 X ELiTE, both at Advantage Golf Cars. That makes the $17,098 Liberty ELiTE 4.2 that ChatGPT's results surfaced the expensive end of the same dealer's stock.
